2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that land bearing Survey No.387/2 measuring 0.0080 hectare, situated in village Sendri, PH No.46, Tahsil and District Bilaspur (CG) (for short 'the said land') is the ancestral property of the petitioner.

After the death of father and other ancestors of petitioner, mutation proceeding was initiated and name of legal representatives of deceased ancestors were recorded pursuant to the order passed by the Tahsildar on 29.4.2022.

Without initiating proceeding for acquisition of the said land and without paying any amount of compensation to petitioner, the respondents have used the said land for construction of 'Bilaspur-Pathrapali National Highway Road No.111/130'.

Petitioner along with other affected land owners submitted application before the Sub-Divisional Officer (R) -cum- Land Acquisition Officer,
Bilaspur for grant of compensation in lieu of use of their ownership land for construction of national highway road.

Respondent No.4 vide memo dated 28.6.2022 forwarded details of lands along with proposed alignment in map sub- division, to the Project Director (respondent No.2) for initiating land acquisition proceeding.

Another letter was written by respondent No.4 to respondent No.2 for depositing the amount of award and publication of notice of initiating proceeding of acquisition for the left out land used in construction of road.
But, till date the respondent No.2 has not taken step for acquisition of lands already used in construction of national highway road.

3. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that after receipt of notice of this writ petition,
respondent No.2 wrote letter dated 18.4.2023 to respondent No.4 for making available sub-division map etc. and when no response was received, respondent No.2 sent reminder letter on 19.6.2023 seeking map after sub-division of khasra numbers so as to verify and tally with the alignment map available with respondents.
Respondent No.4 vide letter dated 20.6.2023 forwarded sub- division map prepared by the Patwari.

After perusal of the map along with reports available with respondent No.2, it revealed that the map, which was forwarded by respondent No.4 vide letter dated 20.6.2023, does not tally with alignment available.
Therefore, respondent No.2 again wrote letter dated 20.7.2023 to respondent No.4 requesting to trace and indicate affected khasra numbers after sub-division of khasra.

But thereafter there is no response from respondent No.4 and therefore,
respondent No.2 sent reminder letters to respondent No.4 to supply necessary documents and information with respect to left out lands stated to be already utilized for construction of national highway road.
He submits that some more compliance is required on the part of respondent No.4 on the letter sent by respondent No.2.
If the documents asked for are sent, necessary steps will be taken in this regard in accordance with law without any further delay thereafter.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents available in record of writ petition.

5. Grievance of petitioner in this writ petition is that land owned by petitioner was used by respondent No.2 for construction of national highway road without acquiring the same and without paying compensation.

It is not in dispute that before construction of road, acquisition proceedings Badri Prasad vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63950499/
2 were initiated but considering the application submitted by villagers and affected land owners that their lands were also used for construction of national highway road and they were not paid compensation, respondent No.4 sent letter to respondent No.2 for initiating acquisition proceeding in respect of land details of which are mentioned in the letter.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Respondent No.2 has taken cognizance of letter written by respondent No.4 and after verifying the same along with records,
respondent No.2 sought clarification and further information from respondent No.4, which is stated to be still awaited.

6. In view of the above facts and circumstances of the case, as the authorities concerned have already taken cognizance of the application submitted by the land oustees, whose lands stated to be used for construction of road but left out in the acquisition proceeding, and claims of such land affected owners are in the process of consideration, in the opinion of this Court, no useful purpose will be served in keeping this writ petition pending, awaiting reply of the respondent State and it can be disposed of at this stage.
7.

Accordingly, writ petition is disposed of directing respondent No.4 to respond to letters written by respondent No.2 dated 2.8.2023 & 11.8.2023 requesting supply of additional material and documents in pursuance of the letter dated 20.6.2023 expeditiously, preferably within a period of three months from the date of receipt of this order.

Respondent No.2 is also directed to take necessary steps after receipt of details of land and other relevant materials from respondent No.4 expeditiously, preferably within an outer limit of further two months thereafter.
8. It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the claim of petitioner and it will be for the concerned authority to take decision in accordance with law.
9. With the above observation and direction, this writ petition stands disposed.
10. Certified as per rules.
